subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs. Competitors — next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@omniva.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs. Competitors — next steps

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for a great session today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum going: 

Key pain points you reiterated:
- Latency spikes during peak batch processing windows (10–12pm ET) impacting user-facing search flows.
- High per-token inference cost that makes conversational experiences hard to scale.
- Need for strict data isolation and audit logs for regulated datasets.

What we heard as success criteria for your evaluation:
1) Median tail latency (p95) under 350ms for interactive chat at 512 tokens.
2) End-to-end cost-per-session reduction of at least 30% vs current provider.
3) SOC 2–equivalent audit trail and KMS integration for encryption of customer prompts.
4) Seamless fallback in case a dedicated cluster health degrades.

Summary of comparative findings (high level):
- Redwood: competitive p95 latency in our dedicated config, strong autoscaling controls, built-in KV/prefix caching for repeat queries. Includes KMS integration and audit logs.
- Competitor A: slightly better single-request latency in demo, but limited autoscaling policies and no per-route cost breakdown.
- Competitor B: cheaper on list price, but required significant engineering for data isolation and no out-of-the-box audit logs.

Open questions we agreed to validate with tests:
- Can you share a 24-hour sample of request patterns (timestamps + token counts) so we can simulate realistic batching? (Evan: file pointer ok)
- Which queries in the sample set are most latency-sensitive vs. tolerant?
- Any compliance docs or DPA clauses we should pre-stage with legal?

Proposed follow-up tests (we can run from our side):
1) 24-hour synthetic load replay using your sample workload to show p50/p95/p99 under Redwood Dedicated.
2) Cost modeling for both dedicated and hosted options for a projected 5M tokens/month baseline.
3) A smoke integration demonstrating KMS key wrap and audit log entries for a subset of traffic.

Next steps / timeline:
- Samantha to share workload sample and legal contact by Thu 9/17.
- Redwood to provide initial synthetic replay results and cost model by Tue 9/22.
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up demo to review results (proposed: Wed 9/23).

Attachments: I uploaded a quick bake-off scoring template (omniva-bakeoff-scores.xlsx) and our short notes (redwood-bakeoff-notes.pdf) to the shared Drive link below.

Happy to adjust priorities if the team wants a different test first.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0147

From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@omniva.ai>

Cc: Evan Li <evan.li@omniva.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs. Competitors — next steps

Thanks Aditya — this is perfect and aligned with our notes. A couple quick clarifications: 

- We can share the anonymized 24-hour trace by EOD Thu 9/17 (I will send via secure Drive link).
- The most latency-sensitive queries are the customer-facing search (approx 40% of requests) and a small set (~5%) of low-latency fraud checks. The rest are batch summarization jobs that tolerate higher latency.
- Legal: please include a copy of your standard DPA and SOC 2 attestation; I’ll share our contract counsel contact in the next email.

Also, can you confirm whether the synthetic replay will include cold-start/no-cache scenarios? We want to see both warm (cached KV) and cold behavior.

Samantha Ortiz
Head of AI Platform
Omniva
Samantha.ortiz@omniva.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@omniva.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs. Competitors — next steps

Thanks Samantha — quick note on cold vs warm: our replay will run two phases:
1) Cold run (no KV/prefix cache warmers) to measure worst-case latency.
2) Warm run after simulated steady-state to show typical p95 with caching and batching effects.

We will also provide p50/p95/p99 breakdowns and breakdown by route (search vs summarization vs fraud checks).

I’ll kick off the replay once we have the anonymized trace. Aditya — I added two items to the scoring sheet: "SLA fallbacks" and "per-route cost granularity."

Marissa Cole
